_meta.description: Core types whose CONTRACT changed across an Elgg major (interface -> abstract class, class -> interface, instantiable class -> interface, or removed entirely) such that a plugin's `implements`/`extends`/`use`/`new` of it that was valid below the boundary becomes a FATAL at or beyond it. Used by PostMigrationVerifier::checkChangedClassContracts() to flag the 'cannot implement X - it is not an interface' (and dual) class of boot fatals that the shape-based completeness gate AND checkRemovedFunctions() are both blind to — the type still exists (or existed) only its kind changed. Caught empirically by bin/verify-migration-chain.sh at the 5x->6x tier on 2026-06-05 (hypeDiscovery/hypeScraper/hypeSeo/hypeMaps upgrade Batch classes).
_meta.method: Batch verified against the installed vendor: 6.x+ ships Elgg\Upgrade\Batch as `abstract class Batch`, with `abstract class AsynchronousUpgrade extends Batch` and `abstract class SystemUpgrade extends Batch` as the concrete contracts. Elgg\Upgrade\Locator::getBatch() only requires is_subclass_of($class, Batch::class), so `extends AsynchronousUpgrade` (or `extends Batch`) is correct; `implements Batch` fatals. Hook / ServiceFacade / NotificationEvent reconstructed from this project's .wolf/cerebrum.md Do-Not-Repeat where each produced a real boot fatal during a bodyology plugin migration.
_meta.cumulative: Treated like removed-functions.json: a contract change at 6.x still applies when targeting 7.x.
_meta.gate_model_note: The gate flags a line only when the type is referenced (via `use FQN;` or inline FQN) AND the entry's `illegal_keyword` co-occurs with the type name on that line. So `illegal_keyword` must name a token that is ALWAYS wrong for the changed type at/after the boundary (e.g. `use` for a removed class, `new` for a class-turned-interface), never a token that is still legal for correctly-migrated code — otherwise the gate emits false positives. See references/migration-failure-catalog.md for two contract-shaped fatals (Seed missing getType()/getCountOptions(); route:rewrite firing at boot) that are deliberately NOT injected here because the keyword gate cannot express them without false-positiving correctly-migrated code — they need a dedicated verifier check.

false_positive_guard_examples.Elgg\\HooksRegistrationService\\Hook: the 4.x concrete hook class — NOT flagged by the Elgg\Hook entry because the FQN prefix `Elgg\Hook` is followed by `s` (Hooks...) so the \b word-boundary fails to match
false_positive_guard_examples.Elgg\\Notifications\\SubscriptionNotific: the concrete 4.x subclass — NOT flagged by the NotificationEvent entry because the file imports SubscriptionNotificationEvent (a different FQN), so the inline-FQN reference check for Elgg\Notifications\NotificationEvent never matches

Elgg\\Di\\ServiceFacade.was: trait (self-registration hook via a name() method)
Elgg\\Di\\ServiceFacade.fix: Remove `use Elgg\Di\ServiceFacade;` (the import) and the in-class `use ServiceFacade;` trait use, plus the `name()` method, from any service class. Register the service with DI\create() in elgg-services.php and use the DI array key as the service name directly. The trait does not exist in Elgg 4.x.

Elgg\\Notifications\\NotificationEvent.fix: `new Elgg\Notifications\NotificationEvent(...)` throws 'Cannot instantiate interface' in 4.x. Use a concrete implementation: Elgg\Notifications\SubscriptionNotificationEvent (object-subscription events) or Elgg\Notifications\InstantNotificationEvent (instant/direct notifications).

Elgg\\Upgrade\\Batch.fix: Replace `implements Batch` with `extends \Elgg\Upgrade\AsynchronousUpgrade` (for admin-run upgrades) or `extends \Elgg\Upgrade\SystemUpgrade`. In 3.x-5.x Batch was an interface; in 6.x it became an abstract class, so `implements Batch` fatals on boot with 'cannot implement Elgg\Upgrade\Batch - it is not an interface'.

Elgg\\Hook.fix: \Elgg\Hook was removed in 6.x (in 5.x it extended \Elgg\Event). Replace `use Elgg\Hook;` -> `use Elgg\Event;`, type-hint `\Elgg\Event $event` instead of `Hook $hook`, and `$hook->getValue()` / `$hook->getParam('k')` -> `$event->getValue()` / `$event->getParam('k')`. Rename any local `$event = $hook->getParam('event')` to `$notification_event` to avoid a collision with the renamed parameter.
